steps.title: Choose a text and question
steps.text: Read the original passage and the question. Identify the aspect the question asks you to discuss.

steps.title: Build your paragraph
steps.text: Choose a claim, drag a relevant quotation into Evidence, then select an explanation and a so-what statement that connect back to the question.

steps.title: Check and improve
steps.text: Read the self-check rubric and revisit any weak link between claim, evidence and explanation. This is practice feedback, not an official grade.

steps.title: Read the passage
steps.text: Read the unfamiliar text and its question before selecting language features.

steps.title: Connect technique and effect
steps.text: Tag a technique, explain its effect in this passage and link it to the writer’s idea. Use the text as evidence.

steps.title: Evaluate your explanation
steps.text: Use the lesson prompts to check that your response explains how the language works, rather than simply naming a technique.

steps.title: Choose an equation
steps.text: Start on the first topic and read the equation and the worked guidance.

steps.title: Change one step
steps.text: Use the available controls to manipulate the equation. Compare the new expression with the previous one and explain why equality is preserved.

steps.title: Test yourself
steps.text: Open Test yourself and use Check to review your answer. Return to the notes when a step is unclear.

steps.title: Start with a tangent
steps.text: Choose the tangent topic and move the input. Compare the point on the curve with the slope readout.

steps.title: Connect the rule and graph
steps.text: Change one control at a time and compare the derivative feedback with the graph. Read the notes for the rule being used.

steps.title: Apply and check
steps.text: Try the linked-rate or derivative questions at your selected level, then use Test yourself to check your reasoning.

steps.title: Choose a mechanism topic
steps.text: Start with the first engine topic. Read the caption to see which part or relationship you are investigating.

steps.title: Change one setting
steps.text: Use the controls under the model and watch the linked numbers. Explain how the piston movement or force changes with that setting.

steps.title: Explain and check
steps.text: Read the exam line and trap, then try Test yourself. The prepared AR piston is static; return to this lesson for motion and calculations.
